messages:
maria: Heads up — we saw an ECC/Xid burst that triggered our node cordon logic in eu-west1 tonight. 3 nodes auto-tainted and are stuck in DRAINING for >20m.
infra-bot: detected: gpu_ecc_spike on node gpu-eu-west1-113, gpu-eu-west1-117, gpu-eu-west1-121; action: taint + drain-start (reason: ECC spike) :warning:
maria: The odd part — Slurm jobs on those nodes didn't migrate because the drain hook waits for job completion (max 30m). Some are long-running training jobs.
jake: Do we have a reconcile loop that force-evicts after a grace window? I thought we had a fallback to preempt.
sophie: We do but it only runs for k8s pods, not Slurm. Slurm's graceful scancel is a different flow. Right now it's blocking the node from leaving service.
oncall: seeing corollary in dataplane: requests routed to fallback pool but capacity is tight so latency spikes for a small % of requests.
samir: Proposal: add a repairwalk reconciler that checks cordoned nodes, inspects orchestration (k8s vs slurm), and runs a staged eviction: 1) gentle scancel (SIGUSR1) 2) wait 2m 3) scancel -t 60 (soft) 4) hard kill + fence.
leo: Agree. Also need better observability — annotate the node with the reconciler run id and reason, so we don't double-run.
maria: Example scancel snippet we can use in the reconciler:
```
# gentle: ask job to checkpoint
scontrol update JobId=12345 TimeLimit=00:30:00
kill -USR1 $(pgrep -f train.py)
sleep 120
scontrol cancel 12345
```
jake: For k8s pods we can use:
```
kubectl taint nodes N key=ECC:NoSchedule --overwrite
kubectl drain N --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# if drain hangs, force after 3m
kubectl cordon N; kubectl delete pod -l instance=long-job --force --grace-period=0
```
sophie: Two caveats: 1) force deleting without checkpointing will cause model training to lose progress (expensive). 2) Some jobs rely on local NVMe cache so delete loses artifacts.
oncall: Cost/priority question — should we prefer preemptible spare capacity for non-critical jobs vs hard-fencing a node? We lost some throughput during this incident.
samir: We can add a cost-aware policy: mark jobs by priority label (team/priority) and try migration to dedicated spare pool for high-priority, preemptible for low-priority. If no capacity, escalate to hard fence after N attempts.
leo: Implementation plan for reconciler:
- detect cordoned node
- inspect running workloads (k8s pods + slurm squeue)
- attempt graceful handover (ckpt/handover) for up to 10m
- attempt soft eviction (scancel soft / kubectl drain with grace)
- if still present, set fencing flag and call hardware ops (power off + replace)
- emit events to pager if >2 nodes in same AZ within 30m
maria: We should also add a safety to avoid cascading evictions in the same rack — do a locality check before fencing more than 1 node in the rack.
jake: Tests: create a simulated ECC spike in staging, run the reconciler, assert that nodes end up in FENCED state only after fallback actions and that Slurm jobs are either checkpointed or cancelled.
sophie: I'll open a PR for the reconciler (golang), and add integration tests in staging slurm cluster. Will add a feature flag to enable for eu-west1 only at first.
maria: Thanks. Also add a short runbook for oncall: when reconciler starts fencing, it should include links to affected job ids + recommended stakeholders (team slack handles).
oncall: +1. Please add a metric: reconciler_runs_total{outcome="graceful|soft_kill|fenced"} and a gauge for nodes_in_repairwalk.
samir: I'll stub metrics and the cost-aware routing policy. Let's avoid automatic hard-fence during business hours for high-util clusters — add an SLO-aware hold window.
leo: FYI I'll add a small debounce to the health signal pipeline to avoid repeated ECC bursts triggering multiple reconciler runs for the same node within 5m.
maria: Great. Sophie — ping me the PR link when ready and I'll review the SLAs and runbook entries.
sophie: Will do. Opening ticket: INFRA-8243 — "repairwalk reconciler for mixed Slurm/K8s drains". Tagging @maria @samir :rocket:
infra-bot: ticket created: INFRA-8243 (Priority: P2) — https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/INFRA-8243 :white_check_mark:
maria: Awesome. We'll monitor tonight and keep the fallback off for eu-central until we validate staging.
oncall: Noted. I'll mute pager for low-priority during the staged rollout and rely on metrics + dashboard alerts.
samir: I'll add a dashboard panel for 'nodes in repairwalk' + per-az correlation so we can spot hardware cluster issues early.
leo: Thanks everyone — squad will iterate on PR + tests. If anything spikes again, call out and we'll accelerate the fence flow. :thumbsup:
